title: EXP-037 — Custom Form Event and Prompt Handler Recovery Across Save and Close/Reopen
objective: On the existing User-scoped Form FX_SingleButtonLab01, first verify the exact Form version and the untouched baseline of its sole Button FX_SingleButton01. Define one custom form event named FX_ButtonPromptEvent01 with exactly one associated event-handler action using the Prompt response type and literal prompt message 'Factory Test Prompt'. Assign the existing Button's Primary event to FX_ButtonPromptEvent01. Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save after configuration, verify the Designer is clean, close only the target Form tab, and reopen the same User-scoped Form through a supported Designer path. Verify that the custom event, Prompt handler configuration, and Button Primary-event assignment are recovered unchanged, alongside the existing Button properties. If the saved Form is safely accessible in the Web Client, optionally click the Button exactly once, observe the Prompt, and dismiss it without changing application data. Limit conclusions to the observed Form-definition recovery and, if tested, runtime Prompt behavior.

in_scope: Repository-only prerequisite review before browser activity: AGENTS.md, EXP-036, EXP-036-R2, the existing component recipes, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt3.md, transcripts/raw/raw-hello-world-pt3.txt, docs/mongoose/guides/form-events.md, and docs/mongoose/guides/form-event-response-types.md. Confirm the actual repository paths and reconcile the documented event/handler workflow before mutation.
Use the existing operator-authenticated Mongoose session. Verify a functional Web Designer in User editing scope without reauthentication.

Locate FX_SingleButtonLab01 using a supported Designer Form-selection or recent-forms path. Verify Name, ScopeType=User, and ScopeName. Stop if the intended User-scoped version cannot be identified unambiguously.

Capture the initial clean Form and component baseline. Confirm exactly one existing native Button, FX_SingleButton01, under the expected Form layout, with Caption='Factory Test Button', component type Button and displayed style Type=PushButton.

Inspect the existing Button Events properties and Form Details Event Handlers list before mutation. Verify that FX_ButtonPromptEvent01 does not already exist and that the Button's Primary event can be assigned without replacing unrelated behavior. If a conflicting assignment or definition exists, stop.

Using the documented Web Designer Form Details > Event Handlers workflow, establish the custom form event FX_ButtonPromptEvent01 with exactly one associated event-handler action. Set its response Type to Prompt.

Configure the Prompt using the supported parameters described in the local guide. Use exact literal message 'Factory Test Prompt'. Prefer a single dismissible OK response, without defining secondary event actions or follow-up processing. If the supported editor requires incompatible configuration, stop rather than broaden the experiment.
Select FX_SingleButton01 and assign the exact event FX_ButtonPromptEvent01 to its Events > Primary property. Preserve Name, Caption, Type, layout, and all unrelated Button properties.

Before Save, capture the rendered Form, selected Button Events > Primary value, event-handler identity, action sequence, response Type=Prompt, and exact configured message. Confirm edits are committed rather than still in inline editors.
Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save following the completed event/handler/Button configuration. Verify that the Designer becomes visibly clean without errors.
Reinspect the saved Form and verify its event name, single Prompt handler action, configured message, Button Primary-event assignment, and original Button properties.
Close exactly FX_SingleButtonLab01 through its ordinary Designer Form-tab close control. Confirm the tab disappears, the Designer remains usable, and no unsaved-changes prompt appears.
Reopen exactly FX_SingleButtonLab01 through an already-supported Designer Form-selection or recent-forms path, without cold URL navigation or an explicit unload.
Verify the reopened Form's Name, User scope, clean state, custom event, Prompt handler, configured literal message, Primary-event assignment, and unchanged Button identity and Caption.

Optionally, after successful definition-recovery verification, open FX_SingleButtonLab01 in the Web Client if the supported route is available without changing session or configuration. Click FX_SingleButton01 exactly once, allow the Prompt handler's asynchronous response to settle, capture the rendered Prompt and message, then dismiss it using its ordinary control. If runtime access is unsafe or unavailable, skip this optional check and record the reason.

Capture planned milestone screenshots and accessibility/property observations with concise evidence summaries under evidence/EXP-037/. Allow no more than one additional fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection for ambiguity recovery.
Write repository documentation only to experiments/EXP-037-custom-form-event-and-prompt-handler-recovery-acro.md and evidence/EXP-037/.
Perform a final read-only audit of the recovered event/handler/Button configuration, lifecycle action counts, repository confinement, recovery allowance, and limitations.

Testing business transactions or writing runtime application data.
Testing Prompt response-button follow-up events or chaining additional handlers.
Database serialization, cache eviction, server-side durability, or independent backend-session recovery.

acceptance_checks.description: Repository-review evidence identifies the exact Hello World Part 3 event/handler workflow and relevant predecessor recipes before browser mutation. Independent browser preflight confirms an authenticated, usable Designer in User scope, no session-establishment prompt, and a clean state. Capture the actual Form scope.

Before mutation, rendered evidence identifies exactly FX_SingleButtonLab01 in User scope with matching ScopeName. The Form is clean and contains exactly one existing Button, FX_SingleButton01, with Caption Factory Test Button, component type Button and style Type PushButton. Capture the Button's current Primary-event value and event-handler list. Prove no FX_ButtonPromptEvent01 collision or conflicting assignment.

Before Save, the Form Details Event Handlers UI visibly identifies FX_ButtonPromptEvent01 with exactly one action sequence configured to the Prompt response type. The supported editor shows literal prompt text Factory Test Prompt. Record every relevant visible field, including any required Prompt parameters.

Before Save, the selected Button's property grid shows Events > Primary = FX_ButtonPromptEvent01. The existing Button Name, Caption, component Type, and rendered layout are unchanged. Evidence identifies the exact target Form and User editing scope.

After the event and Primary-property edits are visibly committed, exactly one ordinary Designer Save is performed. The Designer returns to a visibly clean state without error. Post-Save rendered/property evidence still shows the event, its single Prompt handler action, exact message, Primary-event assignment, and unchanged Button baseline.

Exactly one ordinary Form-tab close removes FX_SingleButtonLab01 from the Designer, with no unsaved-changes prompt. The Designer remains usable. Evidence identifies the Form immediately before closure and shows the tab absent afterward.

Exactly one supported Designer reopen loads FX_SingleButtonLab01, showing the same Name, ScopeType=User and ScopeName. The reopened Designer is clean. No additional Save, Regenerate, explicit unload, or session replacement occurs during reopening.

Post-reopen rendered Form Details and selected-Button property evidence recover exactly one FX_ButtonPromptEvent01 event with one Prompt handler action and message Factory Test Prompt. The Button's Primary event remains FX_ButtonPromptEvent01, and Name, component Type, style Type, Caption and component count match the pre-Save baseline. Classify this as observed Form-definition recovery across ordinary close/reopen, not database durability.

Optional runtime check, gated by safe supported Web Client access: exactly one click on FX_SingleButton01 produces a rendered Prompt showing Factory Test Prompt after event processing settles. Its normal dismiss control closes it, with no runtime application data change. Capture the Form identity, Button, Prompt text, and dismissal. If the runtime gate is unavailable, record not_applicable with the reason; do not fail the otherwise successful definition-recovery experiment solely because this optional check was skipped. If runtime activation is performed but produces a different result, record that discrepancy rather than claiming runtime behavior verified.

Final audit reconciles zero new Forms, zero new Buttons, exactly one custom form event with one Prompt handler action, one Button Primary-event assignment, one ordinary post-configuration Save, one target Form close, and one target Form reopen. If the optional runtime test occurred, count one Button activation and one Prompt dismissal. Evidence establishes no prohibited mutation, session replacement, preference change, or unload. Worker-authored repository writes are confined to the EXP-037 record and evidence directory; automatically generated tool artifacts are disclosed separately. Record the recovery allowance and all limitations.

initial_instruction: T1 — Repository-only prerequisite review. Do not call browser tools or mutate Mongoose. Read AGENTS.md; EXP-036 and its decisive evidence; EXP-036-R2 and its blocker; the verified component recipes; docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt3.md; the raw Part 3 transcript at transcripts/raw/raw-hello-world-pt3.txt; and docs/mongoose/guides/form-events.md and form-event-response-types.md. Confirm the exact local paths and documented Web Designer workflow for a custom form event, its single Prompt handler action, the required Prompt parameters, and Button Events > Primary. Distinguish form events from Application Event System events. Verify whether the Prompt editor supports a single dismissible response without secondary events, and record any uncertainty. Identify the precise existing Form and Button baseline from EXP-036. Write the review and planned evidence matrix only under evidence/EXP-037/ and the experiment record. Stop after this read-only task for coordinator review; do not start browser preflight or modification.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261010-005147-a4PQ. Rationale: EXP-036 successfully created FX_SingleButtonLab01 and verified that its single Button, FX_SingleButton01, retained its Name, Type and Caption across ordinary Designer Save and Form close/reopen. EXP-036-R2 was blocked because the Classic BuildFromScratch wizard failed before Form creation. Rather than retrying the blocked procedure, this experiment introduces one new capability on an existing factory-owned Form: custom form-event handling with a Prompt response and Button Primary-event wiring. The experiment follows the operator-selected Infor Hello World Part 3 tutorial and converted guides, adapted to User editing scope and FX_-prefixed artifacts. The result will be an original observation, not replay verification. | Operator review: record paths aligned, exact-value and no-JavaScript guards added; approved via operator auto-approval 2/3 (2026-10-10). Standard EXP-036 Designer steps apply: select a tab before acting on it (background tabs do not render); Designer footer shows ScopeType/ScopeName; string-resource comboboxes take a literal value plus Enter without choosing a resource; ExtJS checkboxes toggle via their visible label.
